name: anonymous-install-e2e
body: Anonymous-install e2e: the CI check that the public install channels work with no GitHub credentials. `e2e/install_test.go` (`TestAnonymousPackageInstall`, with helpers such as `anonymousEnv`/`installedVersion`) runs the real package-manager install — on macOS, Homebrew tap (`brew tap really-knows-ai/kalide https://github.com/really-knows-ai/kalide`), then the tap-level trust step `brew trust really-knows-ai/kalide`, then `brew install kalide`; on Windows, Scoop bucket + `scoop install kalide` — or the anonymous release download (Linux) with every GitHub token env var (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN`, `KALIDE_GITHUB_TOKEN`) removed, and asserts the installed `kalide` reports the expected version. The macOS setup must run `brew trust really-knows-ai/kalide` before `brew install kalide`: Homebrew 6.0.0+ refuses to load a formula from the untrusted custom-remote tap otherwise, which is exactly how the v0.5.0 package-install-e2e failed. It is wired into CI by the `package-install-e2e` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (owned by solution.component.release-workflow), which runs `go test ./e2e -run TestAnonymousPackageInstall` after the manifest commit; it is not run by the native-e2e workflow. It covers global.constraint.anonymous-install and the homebrew-install / scoop-install / linux-install acceptance criteria. The native-binary init/start e2e (TestNativeRelease) stays in solution.component.native-e2e-ci.
